craft_notes: Sthāyin: adbhuta of all-containing light; vyabhicāri wonder at darkness included, never opposed; FIRST VERSE — sets the house voice (catalogue → oneness → fall; owner verdict required). Sanskrit-first: anastamita (NEVER-SETTING — kept; setting/not-setting is the doctrine); antarbahis (within — kept ‘within/in whom’, personal ground). Rows: 9 (bright-powers/darknesses catalogue held whole), 1 (‘fall’ closes — shine-and-shadow FALL: falling cadence), 5 (stotra-opening tread), 12 (śānta-fall close). Close: ‘shine and shadow fall’. Rupture: semicolon after ‘all’ (catalogue turns to oneness). Rejected: ‘never-fading’ — killed: setting is the doctrine-word; ‘in which’ smoothing — killed: ‘in whom’ keeps the personal ground; ‘gleam and gloom’ — killed: rhyme-twist smuggling tone. Read aloud: LIGHT-nev-er-SET-ting — BRIGHT-pow-ers, DARK-ness-es, ALL … ONE, with-IN, in-WHOM each SHINE and SHA-dow FALL.

lines: Light never setting — bright powers, darknesses, all;
one, within, in whom each shine and shadow fall.
l4.sanskrit_cite: anastamitabhārūpas tejasāṃ tamasām api | ya eko 'ntar yadantaś ca tejāṃsi ca tamāṃsi ca

reads_against.argmap: What never sets, and who dwells within it? → The all-containing One: light that never sets, holding bright and dark.
c1_essence: Unsetting light holds bright and dark alike; one inward reality bounds both.
